questions.q: Do you often change your daily routine?
questions.answer: Not much during the week, as my working hours are fairly fixed. I do try to vary my weekends, though, because doing exactly the same thing every day can make life feel a bit [[stale]].

questions.q: Do you welcome change in your life?
questions.answer: Cautiously, yes. I'm comfortable with routine, but I've learned that a bit of change usually leads to growth. So even when it feels [[daunting]] at first, I try to see it as an opportunity rather than a threat.

questions.q: Has anything changed in your life recently?
questions.answer: Yes, my father retired recently after running his business for over thirty years. It's been a real [[period of adjustment]] for the whole family, since he's at home all day now, but it's lovely to see him finally relaxing.

questions.q: Is there anything you would like to change about your life?
questions.answer: I'd like to study abroad at some point, which would be a big change. After years of helping other students do it, I feel ready to step out of my own [[comfort zone]] and experience it myself.

questions.q: Do you think older people find change harder than young people?
questions.answer: Generally, yes, though not always. My grandfather is in his eighties and still [[remarkably adaptable]], and he even video calls my sister in Dhaka. But many older people understandably feel more secure with familiar routines.
